examples.expected_output: empty DataFrame, i.e. df.query("i == 1.5") / df.loc[[]] — no integer row can equal 1.5
examples.buggy_output_reported: matched the row holding 2 (the value 1.5 is ROUND_HALF_EVEN-rounded to 2, then `i == 2` is applied)

examples.expected_output: rows holding 2 and 3, i.e. df.query("i > 1.5") == df.loc[[1, 2]]
examples.buggy_output_reported: skipped the row holding 2 (compares `i > 2`, returning only the row holding 3)

examples.expected_output: every row, since no row equals 1.5, i.e. df.query("i != 1.5") == df.loc[[0, 1, 2]]
examples.buggy_output_reported: dropped the row holding 2 (compares `i != 2`, returning only rows 1 and 3)

examples.buggy_output_reported: does not match df.loc[[1]] (the non-whole member 1.5 is rounded to 2 and compared)

examples.buggy_output_reported: rounded to 2 and compared as `i > 2`, skipping the row holding 2

examples.input: @pytest.mark.parametrize(op in [==, !=, <, <=, >, >=], value in [1.5, 2.5, -1.5, -0.5], indexed in [True, False]); df = pd.DataFrame({"i": [-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3]}); select("t", where=f"i {op} {value}")
examples.expected_output: tm.assert_frame_equal(result, df.query(f"i {op} {value}")) — comparison as if unrounded
examples.buggy_output_reported: compares against the ROUND_HALF_EVEN-rounded value, so the result disagrees with the unrounded query for at least one value per operator (2.5 rounds down, 1.5 rounds up, so `>= 2.5` and `>= 1.5` are wrong in opposite directions)
